title: fix(plugin-security): a platform operator's insert with no active organization gets the ADR-0123 D2 403, not a 500
body:
Fixes #24821

Clause-②: no

## What changed

A platform operator (the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` rung, `admin_full_access`) whose session has no active organization sent a create on a tenant object whose posture lets the operator cross the organization wall (`access.default: 'private'`, ADR-0095 D3). Under `group` and `isolated` it got `500 ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`. It now gets the answer a member gets in the same state: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, with a message that names the missing active organization (ADR-0123 D2/D4).

The fix is in `plugin-security`'s Layer 0 write wall, `security-plugin.ts` step 3.7, and nowhere else:

- **Why the operator reached the engine.** Crossing makes the operator's own Layer 0 `null` on such an object. So neither the D2 pre-test (`organizationWallRefusal`) nor the union-scope insert arm from #24784 reached it. The row then met the engine's organization check (`resolveSystemInsertOrganization`, ADR-0131 D9) as an organization-less system write, which refuses with a fixed 500 and keeps the prose off the wire.
- **The new arm.** An insert from a caller that crosses the wall and has no `tenantId` is judged on its stored image, in the same `postHookWriteImageCheck` seam and with the same D2 throw (`refuseNoActiveOrganization`) as the #24784 arm. The seam runs after the `beforeInsert` chain and before the engine's organization check. One row with no organization refuses the whole write.
- **The crossing fact.** `computeLayeredRlsFilter` now also returns `crossedByPlatformAdmin`. It asks the one Layer 0 ladder (`computeTenantLayer0Verdict`) a second time with only `isPlatformAdmin` withheld: the verdict is `none`, and it would not be `none` without the exemption. No rung of the ladder (posture, tenant object, phantom anchor, tenancy opt-out) is re-derived. `computeWriteTenantWall` hands step 3.7 the filter and the fact from one computation.
- **Not touched.** `organizationWallRefusal`, `callerHasOrganizationScope`, the union-scope arm, the forge guard, `tenant-layer.ts`, and everything in `packages/objectql`. No new error code. The engine's 500 still answers system contexts, which are what it was written for.

## Why this answer (governing text)

- **ADR-0131 D9** decides the outcome: "a write on a tenant-column object with no organization is derived under `single` … and refused otherwise, with a message naming what is missing (ADR-0123 D4). ⛔ Nothing defaults to any owner other than the derivable one." No governing text lands an operator's organization-less insert anywhere. I searched ADR-0123, ADR-0131 (D5, D9, D12 item 12) and the security plugin's docblocks. So the insert was already refused; this changes the answer, not the outcome.
- **The answer.** The condition is the member's: no active organization, and a new row with nowhere to land. One condition gets one spelling (ADR-0112 D3), the D2 403. The 500 also failed D9's own "message naming what is missing" for an HTTP caller, because a 5xx withholds its prose. The `[#12974]` note in `computeLayeredRlsFilter` already records an org-less write by the platform owner as "REFUSED 403 … (500 where the 403 refusal belongs)".
- **The fork, reported, not resolved by code.** ADR-0123 D2's scope paragraph says the refusal fires for a caller "who is not a platform operator crossing the wall by ADR-0095 D3", and its Consequences list "Platform operators" under "What does not change". That text predates ADR-0131 D9, which refuses this write anyway. The runtime is now wider than that sentence, in the same way #24784's arm made it wider than D2's "empty membership set" sentence. #24823 is the open card for that amendment note. This PR changes no ADR text (`docs/adr/**` is Tier H).

## Measured (real stack: ObjectQL + SqlDriver + SecurityPlugin)

Before, at `4be728131` (the pin alone, committed as `743cacb33` and unchanged since): `Tests 4 failed | 12 passed (16)`. The four failures, under both `group` and `isolated`, were the single and bulk operator inserts: `expected 'ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED' to be 'PERMISSION_DENIED'`. Every control was already green.

After: the operator's insert gets exactly the member's outcome on the same object (`code`, `status` and message compared whole), and nothing is stored. These are unchanged, each pinned per posture:

- the operator WITH an active organization is admitted, and the row lands there;
- a row a `beforeInsert` hook places in an organization is admitted (the stored image is judged, not the session);
- the operator's update of an existing row is admitted, and the row keeps its organization;
- the operator's insert into an object that opted out of tenancy is admitted;
- the operator's read spans every organization;
- a system context with no organization still gets the engine's own `500 ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED`.

Also measured at base (scratch file, not committed): a payload that names `organization_id` is stripped by the engine for a session on a business object, so the operator's org-less insert naming one was a 500 as well. It is now the same 403.

## Tests

- New `no-active-organization-insert-platform-operator.test.ts`: the real-stack pin above, one block per posture, with the member's D2 403 as the control.
- `no-active-organization-write-refusal.test.ts`: its control "a true PLATFORM operator crosses the wall on a posture-permitting object" pinned exactly the changed branch, an org-less insert passing the middleware. In the real stack that insert answered 500. It is re-judged as follows:
  - the crossing is now pinned on what it really admits, the operator's UPDATE with no active organization;
  - the operator's INSERT with no active organization is refused with the conforming D2 refusal;
  - an insert of a row that names its organization lands, and so does an insert WITH an active organization;
  - the business-object sibling now refuses both the insert and the update, so the posture-scoping of the exemption stays measured.
- Final head `d366c1712` (the merge of `origin/main` `abd5acdaf`), one locked run: closure build OK; `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security test`: `Test Files 196 passed (196)`, `Tests 4066 passed | 45 skipped (4111)`; `typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck: OK … 0 error(s)`). `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles` compiles both edited test files (196 test files in all).

### Ablations (each one committed first, mutated through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in a script with a restore trap, and restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty)

No build or `dist/` leg was needed: the pins import `./security-plugin.js` relatively, and objectql and driver-sql are source aliases in this package's vitest config.

1. **The arm off.** Anchor `callerCrossesTenantWall &&` was replaced by `/* ABLATION-24821 */ false &&` (anchor x1 to x0, marker x0 to x1, blob `25d6a049` to `9786d9c1`). Result: `Tests 5 failed | 34 passed (39)`, in the predicted direction (red). The four real-stack refusals failed with `Received: "ERR_SYSTEM_WRITE_ORGANIZATION_REQUIRED"`, and the unit refusal failed with `the write was not refused at all`. Every control stayed green.
2. **The crossing discriminator off** (any `none` verdict for an operator counts as a crossing). The second-ladder comparison was replaced by `/* ABLATION-24821-B */ true;` (blob `25d6a049` to `f9b75967`). Result: `Tests 2 failed | 37 passed (39)`, in the predicted direction: the opted-out-of-tenancy control under both postures (`expected the write to be admitted`).

## Gates (local, head `d366c1712`)

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` (no paths) derived 69 commands from the 4 changed paths against merge base `abd5acdaf`. All 69 exit 0, each code captured before any pipe. `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` and `check:i18n` first answered exit 3 `PREREQUISITE NOT MET`, which is not a measurement. After a workspace build (`turbo run build --filter=!@objectstack/docs`, 76/76) both measured exit 0. `--ran`: `69 derived, 69 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN`. The repo-wide runs (`pnpm lint`, `test:repo`) are CI's.

## Acceptance notes (observed, not fixed here)

1. **ADR-0123 D2's scope sentence now under-describes the runtime.** It still says a platform operator crossing the wall is outside the refusal. Carrier: #24823 (its amendment note can name this arm next to the union-scope one). See the open question in the report.
2. **A platform operator's cross-organization by-id update on a posture-permitting object answers 404, while the same caller reads the row.** Measured in-process at `4be728131` on `qa_vault` (private), row in `org_b`:
   - `group` with no active organization: `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`;
   - `group` with active `org_a`: `404`;
   - `isolated` with active `org_a`: `404`;
   - `isolated` with no active organization: `200`.

   `findOne` returns the row in all four. This looks like the engine's by-id write scope being computed over its own facts (no platform-admin fact), against ADR-0131 D8's one predicate. Reach was not measured at a public door. Carrier: none.
3. **The engine's organization check has no `isSystem` test.** Any non-system caller that reaches it without an organization still gets the system-write 500. After #24784 and this PR the wall covers members and crossing operators on every object the wall itself recognises as a tenant object. Populations it may not cover, all unmeasured:
   - an object whose declared `tenancy.tenantField` is not `organization_id`;
   - `systemFields.tenant: false` together with an explicit `organization_id` column;
   - a federated object that declares a real remote `organization_id`;
   - a composition with no security plugin.

   This is the card's second candidate, which is `domain:engine`'s. Carrier: none.
4. **`canWriteObject`'s create preview.** It is row-less, so for this operator it still answers `true` (as it did while the write answered 500). The same boundary #24784 recorded.
